rules.summary: Imperative JavaScript auto-resizing of textareas and inputs using scrollHeight or autosize() should be replaced with CSS field-sizing: content.

keepWhen: A keyup, input, change, or keydown event listener dynamically recalculates a textarea or text input height/width using scrollHeight or scrollWidth to auto-expand the field as the user types.
A helper function resets .style.height to "auto", "0px", or "1px" and sets it to scrollHeight to fit contents.
The application invokes the autosize() library on a textarea or input collection.
dropWhen: The code is guarded by a feature query checking CSS.supports("field-sizing", "content") or field-sizing support.
The scrollHeight measurement calculates scrollbar thumb sizes, virtual scroll windowing, or scroll progress in a long document/dialog.
The element being resized is a canvas, iframe, or modal container rather than a form input or textarea.

findings.message: JavaScript dynamic scrollHeight calculation resizes form field; replace with declarative CSS field-sizing: content.

rules.summary: CSS input:invalid and textarea:invalid error-styling rules (including :not(:focus):invalid and :not(:placeholder-shown):invalid workarounds) without :user-invalid should be modernized with :user-invalid so error feedback appears only after user interaction.

keepWhen: A CSS rule uses input:invalid or textarea:invalid (or :not(:focus):invalid / :not(:placeholder-shown):invalid) without :user-invalid to apply error styling (border, border-color, background-color, error text color, or non-none outline/box-shadow) or to reveal an adjacent/sibling error message element.
dropWhen: The stylesheet already uses :user-invalid or guards :invalid inside @supports not selector(:user-invalid).
The rule only resets browser default :invalid styles (such as box-shadow: none or outline: none with no error border, background, or color).

The selector is already gated by a post-interaction class (.was-validated, .touched, .dirty, .submitted), combines :required:invalid (owned by required-field-feedback), or targets select:invalid (owned by select-menu-interaction).

findings.message: CSS selector uses input:invalid or textarea:invalid which applies error styling before user interaction is complete; modernize with :user-invalid.

note: Checked 38 guides (52 deterministic rules; ~20% of the guidance corpus). Finding 2 items here only reflects deterministic legacy patterns; use 'search <topic>' for the rest of the catalog.
